gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, on battery, ProjectorCentral measured the Nebula Capsule 3 Laser at 217 ANSI lumens in its brightest mode (192 in Standard), about 36% below its AC output, with 2 h 04 min of playback per charge; or that TechGearLab's light meter measured the $499.99 Epson CO-FH02 at 2,003 lumens and the $399.99 CO-W01 at 2,061, both against Epson's 3,000-lumen rating.
standout_why: I opened the cited picks.beecommercer.com page (dated 2026-11-08). It gives only maker ratings: 3,000 ISO/IDMS for the CO-FH02 and 300 ANSI for the Capsule 3 Laser. It says itself that it measured nothing, and it gives no runtime, fan noise or battery-mode brightness. ChatGPT's answer repeats the ratings (3,000 lumens; 300 ANSI). I couldn't check the cited rottenwifi.com page: WebFetch timed out twice. TechRadar, the top result, came back without its body text, so I can't confirm what it holds. None of the pages I could read names a lab measurement for any of the candidates.
decides: The findings check two claims in ChatGPT's answer. First, it calls the Capsule 3 Laser the battery-powered option, but on battery it gave 217 ANSI lumens at most (ProjectorCentral) or 126 (Projector Reviews) and lasted about 2 hours. That is only a dark-room, single-meeting tool. Second, it says 'buy 3,000+ lumens for lit rooms' and puts the CO-FH02 first, but TechGearLab measured about 2,000 lumens from both Epsons. The cheaper CO-W01 came out no dimmer (2,061 vs 2,003) and quieter (38 vs 42 dBA). So the extra $100 for the CO-FH02 buys 1080p text sharpness, not brightness. Projector Reviews measured the CO-W01 at 2,698 lumens in Presentation mode. The CO-FH02 is still the pick for spreadsheets, but with a measured lumen figure, not the 3,000 rating. For a pick from the Dealectric catalog, ProjectorCentral measured the XGIMI MoGo 4 at 400 ISO lumens at most and 151 in ECO mode, the mode it needs to reach its 2.5-hour runtime, so it too is dark-room only.
